headline: Labor unions and AI companies are spending at least $1 million on advertising to push for rules on data centers, the Des Moines Register reports.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: only the headline could be read, so the backers, the states and the ad content are unverified.
importance_line: Voters and local officials in places debating data center limits are the likely audience, and unions and AI companies both gain when data centers are built, but the backers' names, the states and the content of the ads are not known.
summary: The Des Moines Register reports that labor unions and AI companies are pushing for data center guardrails (limits on how the facilities are built and run) in an advertising buy worth seven figures, meaning at least $1 million.
notes: Headline only: the Register page returned 402 and no other outlet carried the ad-buy story. Related, unmerged context: the American Infrastructure Alliance (AIA), a coalition of unions and AI companies launched on 28 Sep 2026, is campaigning for data center guardrails in seven states (Mirror Indy, 5 Oct 2026); the Register's page address contains 'aia', but the link between the two is not confirmed.
